chapter: Cee Pee Johnson, Hampton and the Navy band
title: Leading the Navy band and the Bombadiers at St. Mary's
summary: Royal led the 45-piece Navy band and the 17-piece Bombadiers swing band at St. Mary's Pre-Flight School, with its roster.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: We had a 45-piece military band. I was the leader of the swing band called the Bombadiers, which was a 17-piece band. Vernon Alley was bass player in that particular band.
You had a couple of other people who (inaudible) --
-- (inaudible) names, made some in that band, too.
We had some nice guys in that band.

He was a saxophone player, and Buddy Collette, he was a saxophone player in that band. Jerome Richardson was in the band. Also we had a great saxophone section. There was none better, I would say. It was a good band.
Did you -- were you stationed right -- (inaudible) -- where was it, Oakland?

Right there at St. Mary's Pre-Flight. That was at St. Mary's College and the Pre-Flight Program took over the complete college, everything. Dormitories and everything. And turned out into (inaudible) a Navy Institution. So, it was producing young American manhood for flyers. That's where they learned their beginnings, got their computations straight and learnt their arithmetic and other things before they went into the actual flying.
And you were in the big orchestra and you had the (inaudible)? swing band.
Did you play for only military bands or (inaudible)? did the civilians get to hear you, too?
